plan.summary: BRO-5517 follow-up: six show notes, which print on the /biz show card, still quoted tax credit guesses written before the state paid or allocated the award the recoupment model now counts (scripts/lib/ny-tax-credit.js). Glengarry Glen Ross said "Expected ~$1.9M" (paid $2.7M), An Enemy of the People "~$1.3M" (paid ~$2.3M), Othello "~$2M" and Romeo + Juliet "up to $1.75M" (each allocated $3M); Buena Vista Social Club’s "Eligible for $3M" is now a payment; Art has no award listed and its "Eligible for $3M" named the cap as if owed. Only the tax credit sentence changes in each note. Found by the new taxCreditNoteConflicts check (commercial-record-checks.js warning; audit-commercial-data.js weekly sweep).
steps: Each action replaces one sentence of the notes; the rest of each note is unchanged.
After apply, taxCreditNoteConflicts returns no conflict for any record.

actions.oldValue: Kieran Culkin, Bob Odenkirk, Bill Burr revival (all Broadway debuts). $7.5M cap (SEC confirmed). Recouped in 9 weeks (May 12, 2025). Broke Palace Theatre box-office record ($2.4M gross). Weekly nut ~$925K — early weeks roughly broke even, then $1M+ weeks drove quick recoupment. Expected ~$1.9M NY state tax credit (25% of costs). Run extended twice. All-male cast throughout.
actions.newValue: Kieran Culkin, Bob Odenkirk, Bill Burr revival (all Broadway debuts). $7.5M cap (SEC confirmed). Recouped in 9 weeks (May 12, 2025). Broke Palace Theatre box-office record ($2.4M gross). Weekly nut ~$925K — early weeks roughly broke even, then $1M+ weeks drove quick recoupment. Paid a $2.7M NY tax credit by Jun 2026 (Bloomberg Tax). Run extended twice. All-male cast throughout.
actions.description: glengarry-glen-ross-2025: the note tax credit sentence matches the award the model counts: paid about $2.7M by Jun 2 2026 (Bloomberg Tax, from ESD records), not the ~$1.9M expected.

actions.oldValue: Jeremy Strong and Michael Imperioli in Amy Herzog's Ibsen adaptation. $5.5M cap recouped during run at Circle in the Square (840 seats). Broke CITS weekly gross record 16 times during run. Final week record: $1,266,338 (prev record $917K by Hugh Jackman in The River). Joined Broadway's $1M Club for weekly grosses — almost unheard of for a non-musical. Strong won Tony for Best Actor. Digital lottery + cancellation line ensured 100%+ capacity some weeks. Eligible for ~$1.3M tax credit.

actions.oldValue: Producer Orin Wolf noted it 'only cost $17 million' - modest for 2025 musical. Won 5 Tony Awards. Typical weekly gross $0.9-1.0M at 90-95% capacity. Break-even ~$0.85M. Broadway Journal: 'if they can weather the next year... may recoup in 12-18 months.' Eligible for $3M NY tax credit.

actions.oldValue: Denzel Washington & Jake Gyllenhaal. $9M cap. Recouped in 9 weeks (May 1, 2025). Shattered weekly Broadway play record with $2.82M gross (topping Harry Potter). Premium tickets reached $921. Highest-grossing play revival in world history. Expected ~$2M NY tax credit. 15-week limited run closed day of Tony Awards. Tony snub but producers announced recoupment as rejoinder. Washington likely had gross percentage deal.

actions.oldValue: Kit Connor and Rachel Zegler in Sam Gold's immersive production at Circle in the Square (794 seats). $7M cap recouped during 20-week run — 'rare industry feat' for Shakespeare. Final week $1.48M. Highest-grossing limited engagement in CITS history. 14% of buyers age 18-24 (youngest Broadway audience demographics ever). Jack Antonoff provided music. Sonya Tayeh choreography. Run extended twice. ATP $150-180 via dynamic pricing. SRO tickets sold for additional revenue. Eligible for up to $1.75M tax credit.

actions.oldValue: Bobby Cannavale, James Corden, Neil Patrick Harris revival. $6.75M cap (Broadway News confirmed, SEC 'White Canvas Broadway LP' $6.9M). Recouped week ending Dec 14, 2025 (~13 weeks into 16-week run). Weekly nut ~$725-750K — surprisingly high for 3-actor play due to star salaries (~$350K/week combined) and premium Broadway Journal ad spend. Averaged $1.2-1.8M gross at ~99% capacity. Matthew Warchus directed (also directed original 1996 production). Eligible for $3M NY tax credit.
